svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Smart Estate – wiring alternatives
svg.text: Use what you have. Each option shows the wires and the one line to change at the top of smarthome.ino. Green frame = what the code does now.
Quiet and strong enough for a cardboard gate.
ENA jumper ON (or ENA → GPIO 27 for soft start).
Tiny board, 2.5–12 V, up to 0.8 A.
L293D or TB6612 work the same (IN1/IN2).
Both NC → GND, both NO → motor supply (+).
Relay 1 on = open, relay 2 on = close.
Big MG996R: give it its own 5 V 2 A supply.
End switches for a DC motor (optional)
Motor stops exactly when the gate hits a switch.
GPIO 39 needs a 10 kΩ resistor to 3V3.
Talks with the clips on the SD card.
Never connect the speaker to GND.
Line-out → any amplifier or speaker with AUX.
Use SPK1/SPK2 OR DAC – not both.
No module: beeps, ding-dong, siren, melodies.
Passive piezo: straight on GPIO 4 + GND.
Up to 3 LEDs per pin, each with its OWN resistor.
White/blue: 100 Ω. Max ~20 mA per pin.
Many LEDs: one transistor per room
Up to ~20 LEDs per room from the 5 V rail.
IRLZ44N MOSFET instead: up to 100s of LEDs.
Simplest for lots of LEDs: no extra transistors.
Pin 9 GND, pin 10 COM to 5 V.
Mains bulb (230 V) with a relay module
On/off only. ADULT ONLY: mains can kill.
Closed box, no bare 230 V on the model.
12 V G4 / car bulb or 12 V LED bulb.
Dims like the LEDs. Add 10 kΩ gate → GND.
A transistor or MOSFET gives 3 speeds + breeze.
